title: Noah and the Rainbow Promise
bigQuestion: What does the story of Noah say about choices and promises?

story.title: A Rainbow After the Storm
story.kicker: The storm is over. A rainbow shines. Grandma has a story to tell.
paragraphs: Rain taps on the window. Thunder rumbles far away. Then the storm stops. Maya and her little brother Jon run to the window. The sun peeks out. A rainbow stretches across the sky. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.

Grandma comes to look too. She smiles. "That reminds me of an old story," she says. "It is in the Bible, in a book called Genesis. It is the story of Noah." Maya and Jon sit on the rug. They love Grandma's stories.
Grandma tells how the world got full of unkindness. She tells how Noah listened to God. She tells about a big boat full of animals. Jon giggles at the animal part. "Two by two!" he says.
"And at the end," Grandma says, "the story says God put a rainbow in the sky. It was a sign of a promise." Maya looks back at the window. The rainbow is fading now. But she will remember the story.
story.think: Grandma says the rainbow was a sign of a promise. What is a promise you have made?

lessons.title: Some Heavenly Ones Chose Wrong
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 6 says some heavenly ones chose wrong and came down to earth.
reading: The Bible's first book is *Genesis*. Chapter 6 tells a short, puzzling story. It says the *sons of God* came down to earth. They chose wives from the people there.
Michael Heiser was a teacher. He read the Bible in its old languages. He thought the sons of God were heavenly ones. He said they left their home and chose wrong.
Other readers see it another way. Some think the sons of God were people, not heavenly ones. Readers still talk about this story today.

words.d: the first book of the Bible
a name in Genesis 6; Heiser thought it meant heavenly ones from God's family in heaven

look.title: Genesis 6 in Easy Words
look.text: There were many people on the earth. The sons of God saw the daughters of people. They saw that they were lovely. They chose wives from among them.
look.cite: Genesis 6:1–2, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Who came to the earth in this story? What did they do?

check.q: What did Heiser think the sons of God were?
check.why: Heiser read Genesis 6 and thought the sons of God were heavenly ones who chose wrong.

check.q: Which book of the Bible tells this story?
check.why: The story is in Genesis, chapter 6. Genesis is the Bible's first book.

check.q: What do some other readers think?
choices: The sons of God were birds
The story is about a rainbow
The sons of God were people
check.why: Some readers think the sons of God were people, not heavenly ones.

lessons.title: A World Full of Hurting
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the world filled with hurting and unkindness.
reading: Genesis 6 says things on earth went wrong. People were not kind. They hurt each other. The story says the earth was full of *violence*. That means hurting.
The story says God saw it. God was sad in his heart. The story says God planned a new start for the world.
Heiser thought the heavenly ones who chose wrong made things worse. Their wrong choice spread to people. One wrong choice can lead to more.

words.d: not gentle or caring toward others

look.title: Two Playgrounds
look.text: Look at two playgrounds. On the first one, kids push and grab. Someone is crying. On the second one, kids take turns on the slide. Two kids help a friend who fell down.
look.prompt: Which playground is more like the world the story says God wanted? Why?

check.q: What does the word violence mean?
check.why: Violence means hurting others on purpose. Genesis 6 says the earth was full of it.

check.q: How did God feel when he saw the hurting, the story says?
check.why: Genesis 6 says God was sad in his heart when he saw the hurting.

check.q: What did Heiser think made things on earth worse?
check.why: Heiser thought the heavenly ones' wrong choice spread to people and made things worse.

lessons.title: Noah Chose to Listen
lessons.mainIdea: In the story, Noah listened to God.
reading: One man was different. His name was *Noah*. Genesis 6 says Noah walked with God. That means he stayed close to God and listened.
The story says God told Noah a big flood was coming. God told Noah to build a big boat. The boat would keep Noah's family and many animals safe.
Noah did all that God told him. Genesis 6:22 says so. It can be hard to *listen* when others do not. Noah listened anyway.

words.d: a man in Genesis who listened to God and built a big boat

look.title: Noah Did It All
look.text: Noah did everything God told him to do. He did just what God asked.
look.cite: Genesis 6:22, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What does this verse say Noah did?

check.q: What does "Noah walked with God" mean?
choices: He stayed close to God and listened
check.why: In Genesis 6, walking with God means staying close to God and listening.

check.q: What did God tell Noah to build?
check.why: The story says God told Noah to build a big boat to keep his family and the animals safe.

check.q: Which verse says Noah did all God told him?
check.why: Genesis 6:22 says Noah did everything God told him.

lessons.title: The Big Boat and the Animals
lessons.mainIdea: Noah built a big boat called an ark. Animals came in two by two.
reading: The big boat is called an *ark*. Genesis 6 says it was very long. It was made of wood. It had a roof, a door and three floors inside.
God told Noah to bring animals. Two of each kind came, a male and a female. Some kinds came in sevens. Noah brought food for everyone too.
Noah's family went in too. There was Noah and his wife. There were his three sons and their wives. That makes eight people.

words.d: the big wooden boat Noah built

look.title: Counting on the Ark
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? What does it count?

check.q: What is an ark?
check.why: An ark is the big wooden boat Noah built in Genesis 6.

check.q: How many people were in Noah's family on the ark?
check.why: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their three wives make eight people.

check.q: How did most animals come to the ark?
check.why: Genesis 6 says two of each kind came, a male and a female.

lessons.title: Rain, Then a Dove
lessons.mainIdea: After the rain stopped, a dove brought Noah an olive leaf.
reading: The rain came. Genesis 7 says it fell for forty days and forty nights. Water covered the land. The ark floated on top. Noah's family was safe inside.
Then the rain stopped. The water went down slowly. Noah sent out a *dove*. It came back with an *olive* leaf in its beak. Now Noah knew. Dry land was coming back!
Noah waited for God to tell him. Then his family stepped out onto dry ground. The animals came out too.

words.d: a gentle gray or white bird
a small fruit that grows on a tree with thin green leaves

look.title: The Olive Leaf
look.text: Picture the ark resting on a mountain. The sky is quiet. A little dove flies back to the window. In its beak is a fresh green leaf.
look.prompt: What did the green leaf tell Noah?

check.q: How long did the rain fall in the story?
check.why: Genesis 7 says the rain fell for forty days and forty nights.

check.q: What did the dove bring back?
check.why: Genesis 8 says the dove came back with an olive leaf in its beak.

check.q: Why was the olive leaf good news?
choices: It meant dry land was coming back
check.why: A fresh leaf meant trees were out of the water. Dry land was coming back.

lessons.title: A Promise in the Sky
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 9 says God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign of his promise.
reading: Noah and his family stood on dry land. Then, the story says, God made a *promise*. God promised never again to cover the whole earth with a flood.
God gave a sign of the promise. The sign was a *rainbow* in the clouds. The story says when the rainbow shows, God will remember his promise.
In the Bible, a big promise like this is called a *covenant*. The story says this one was for Noah, his family and every living thing.

words.d: saying you will surely do something
an arc of colors in the sky after rain

look.title: The Bow in the Cloud
look.text: I put my bow in the cloud. It is the sign of my promise with the earth. When the bow is in the cloud, I will remember my promise.
look.cite: Genesis 9:13–15, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What does God say the bow in the cloud is a sign of?

check.q: What did God promise in Genesis 9, the story says?
choices: To send a dove every day
Never again to cover the whole earth with a flood
check.why: Genesis 9 says God promised never again to cover the whole earth with a flood.

check.q: What was the sign of the promise?
check.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow in the clouds is the sign of the promise.

check.q: What is a covenant?
check.why: In the Bible, a covenant is a big, lasting promise, like the one in Genesis 9.

lessons.title: The Book of Enoch
lessons.mainIdea: An old book called 1 Enoch tells more about the heavenly ones. It calls them Watchers.
reading: Genesis 5 tells about a man named Enoch. He lived long before Noah. He was Noah's great-grandfather. The Bible says Enoch walked with God.
Long ago, people wrote an old book about Enoch. It is called *1 Enoch*. Most Bibles do not have it. The Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox churches keep it in their Bible.
1 Enoch tells more about the heavenly ones in Genesis 6. It calls them *Watchers*. Heiser studied this old book closely. He wrote books about it.

words.d: an old book with stories about Enoch and the Watchers
the name 1 Enoch gives to the heavenly ones who chose wrong

look.title: From Enoch to Noah
look.prompt: How many steps is it from Enoch to Noah?

check.q: What does 1 Enoch call the heavenly ones who chose wrong?
check.why: 1 Enoch calls the heavenly ones from Genesis 6 the Watchers.

check.q: Who was Enoch to Noah?
check.why: Genesis 5 goes from Enoch to Methuselah to Lamech to Noah. Enoch was Noah's great-grandfather.

check.q: Which churches keep 1 Enoch in their Bible?
choices: The Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox churches
check.why: Most Bibles do not have 1 Enoch. The Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox churches keep it.

lessons.title: God Keeps Promises
lessons.mainIdea: Both old books say God set things right. The story says God keeps his promises.
reading: In 1 Enoch, God sends good *angels* to help. God tells Noah to get ready. God stops the Watchers from doing more wrong. Then the book looks ahead to a clean, new start.
In Genesis, the rainbow shows up again and again. Each time, the story says, God remembers his promise. Many Jews and Christians see the rainbow as a *reminder* of it.
A promise is something you can count on. Keeping a promise shows care. You can keep promises too, like helping at home or being a good friend.

look.title: Lena's Promise
look.text: Lena told her little sister, "I will read to you tonight." At bedtime Lena is tired. She wants to sleep. Then she remembers her promise. She gets the book and reads.
look.prompt: How did Lena keep her promise? How do you think her sister felt?

check.q: In 1 Enoch, whom does God send to help?
check.why: 1 Enoch tells how God sends good angels to help and to set things right.

check.q: What does the rainbow help people remember, in the story?
check.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise.

check.q: What is a reminder?
check.why: A reminder helps you remember. Many readers see the rainbow as a reminder of the promise.

review.q: Who listened to God and built the ark?
review.why: Genesis 6 says Noah listened to God and built the ark.

review.q: What was the sign of God's promise to Noah?
review.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow in the clouds is the sign of the promise.

review.q: What does 1 Enoch call the heavenly ones who chose wrong?
What did Heiser think the sons of God in Genesis 6 were?
review.why: Heiser thought the sons of God were heavenly ones who chose wrong.

review.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
review.why: Genesis 8 says the dove came back with an olive leaf.

review.q: Which book of the Bible tells about Noah?
review.why: Noah's story is in Genesis, chapters 6 to 9.
